caseDefinition.steps: Open a clean source document with cursor; ordinary external filesystem writes and a separate CLI process each modify in place or atomically replace the file. Independently verify native watch, reactivation and explicit refresh. Deliver stale successes and errors after a newer revision.
caseDefinition.expected: Current real bytes and revision replace the clean base, preserving a reasonable clamped cursor. No old-base save, dirty/conflict approval or CLI-specific approval; stale responses never overwrite newer content.

coverage: Production FileBuffer selection preservation/clamping, clean and conflict state, hash/revision update.
Held real read/metadata delivery success and failure after a newer refresh are discarded by the production sequence guards.

I.chain: Actual macOS FSEvents -> FileWatchService -> bridged IPC event delivery -> FileWorkspaceStore -> FileBuffer -> FileService -> r4 packaged native broker -> independent filesystem bytes/stat checks
coverage: 2 writer forms x 2 modification forms x 3 trigger paths = 12 matrix branches.
4 late-delivery branches: read/metadata x success/error after newer real IO.

Native watcher branches receive actual OS event callbacks and production changed+native updates; other branches deliberately do not attach watchers, proving the intended reactivation/explicit-refresh entry.
Every branch checks source bytes/hash/mtime/inode remain exactly as the external writer left them, zero save and zero checkpoint calls, clean state and no conflict.
In-place writes preserve inode and cursor 22; atomic replacements change inode and clamp cursor to the new text length.

All branches rerun once against the frozen DEV041 FileBuffer; source archive taken before test and all 20 hashes verified afterward.

boundaries: U+I are the explicit required layers in this case; no native App GUI or physical IME result is claimed.

The current TypeScript buffer/store run from the workspace; r4 contributes only packaged native broker/watcher resources. r4 itself does not contain DEV040/DEV041 and is not represented as the tested final App.

Ordinary external writes use the test host filesystem API independently of the production file client. CLI writes run a separate Electron-Node process with fixed script/argv. No model, shell profile, network, user repository or external resource is accessed.
IPC event delivery is bridged at the renderer boundary. OS filesystem events, FileWatchService, FileService, broker, file contents and revisions are real.
Delayed delivery errors are intentional transport-boundary injections after actual native IO, preserving both successful and failing response ordering.
No production files were changed for H15. Formal index and main milestone documents remain owned by the root agent.
